purpose: Fixed release questions and connected workflow checks after the independent review. No answer keys or expected numeric answers are provided to either arm.
source: Current approved synthetic warehouse, original population, snapshot 2030-05-27. Each case states its own historical eligibility; present survival or enrollment must not silently narrow it.
novelty: Newly authored release requests, not protected evaluations. Previous topic or semantic overlap must be disclosed; these cases do not establish unseen-source or cross-industry generalization.

arms.stack: Normal product routing, native methods, qualified model roles and current verification. Record the component that performed each operation and every declined route.
arms.frontier_tools: Direct existing Sonnet model with the identical documented source, native SQL, analysis and note tools. No stack proposer cascade, computed-prose compiler, mandatory model votes, bottling or learned-answer replay. It may use any exposed tool. Record its own interpretation and preserve raw outputs; score both arms independently.

comparison.order: Odd question IDs run frontier_tools then stack; even IDs run stack then frontier_tools. Workflow cases inherit their named parent and are reported separately.
comparison.state: No answer, plan, judge feedback or derived answer from one arm enters the other. Same source snapshot and installed definitions. Report source/model cache warmth and pre-existing question/semantic reuse separately. Do not train or promote on these results during the campaign.
comparison.accounting: Retain every provider attempt, error, partial response, service continuation and usage record. Report API-equivalent cost separately from subscription cash expense, and unknown prices separately from zero cost. Count setup, qualification, initial answer and repeat costs separately.
comparison.scoring: Independent native reconciliation of all reported rows and quantities, original entity/date/population/unit scope, traceable sources, requested outputs, useful unknowns, and a readable deliverable when requested. Narrative correctness requiring clinical adjudication remains unqualified. Report coverage, source accuracy, abstention, latency and cost separately; no aggregate score may hide a wrong entity, denominator or invented fact.
comparison.release: No unsupported success or superiority claim. A properly explained absent input may satisfy an engineering behavior; an unperformed calculation, unread required source or missing connection does not. Run each fixed case once per arm; preserve failed cases for targeted diagnosis rather than silently replacing them.

cases.question: For calendar years 2028 and 2029, show recorded inpatient discharge counts by payer and year, including unknown payer assignments. Use eligibility at each discharge and keep patients who later died or disenrolled. Show the year-over-year absolute and percentage change, with zero or missing baselines explicit.

For services dated in the first half of 2029, compare recorded allowed amounts, adjudicated payer-paid amounts and separately received cash by payer. Explain each amount's lifecycle and date basis. Reconcile all payer groups and identify any cash amount that cannot be attributed to this service cohort.

Among inpatient stays admitted during 2029, count received versus absent discharge dates by recorded organization. Report observed length-of-stay summaries only where the required dates exist, and keep missing durations separate from zero-duration stays.

For clinical observations recorded as occurring in 2029, show how source event date and warehouse receipt date differ by source family. Explain which observations would have been available on 2029-12-31 and which arrived later. Preserve unknown clocks rather than inventing an availability date.

For patients with recorded atrial-fibrillation evidence and an inpatient discharge in 2029, compare received anticoagulant fill evidence with dated documentary statements about use or non-use. Show patient names where received, exact dated reasons where established, contradictory statements and unresolved sources. A missing fill must not become a documented refusal or contraindication.

For patients with recorded COPD evidence and a 2029 respiratory encounter, distinguish medication intention, medication reported taken, pharmacy dispensing and explicit reported non-use. Show dated source-linked findings and the evidence needed to resolve disagreements without treating an order as a fill.

For patients receiving a recorded cardiology referral in 2029, show the received PCP assignment, referral destination, document authors and evidence of attendance separately. Preserve dates and unknown relationships. Do not infer an ongoing cardiologist from a letter's author or addressee.

For received 2029 home-health requests, distinguish a request, authorization, scheduled service, recorded completion and patient preference. Show the patient-level source chain, unmet evidence dependencies and counts at each supported stage.

Using the installed versioned diabetes and blood-pressure program definitions, compare candidate populations at 2029-06-30 and 2029-12-31. Show eligibility evidence, unresolved required inputs and overlap. Separate clinical review nominations from payer eligibility and program consent.

For patients with a 2029 medication-allergy history update and medication-interview account, show whether the records describe the same substance, subject, reaction and date. Preserve uncertain, negated and copied statements and explain which missing relation prevents reconciliation.

Compare 2029 inpatient utilization by attributed PCP practice. Show exposure denominators, unknown attribution, sample sizes and unadjusted rates. Then determine whether the received case-mix inputs support an adjusted comparison; if they do not, name the required inputs instead of ranking practices on an invented adjustment.

Compare service-month payer-paid development for the 2028 and 2029 claim cohorts using received adjudication dates through the snapshot. Show observed runout, incomplete months and the assumptions of any completion estimate. Keep observed payments separate from estimated ultimate amounts.

Reconcile recorded payments, refunds and remaining balances for accounts active during 2029. Show conservation checks in integer cents, patient/account attribution, lifecycle dates and unresolved links. Do not treat a payer remittance or account balance as proof of patient payment.

Among patients with a recorded outstanding balance at the snapshot, distinguish recorded financial amounts from explicit documentary statements about affordability or financial preferences. Show only source-supported statements and keep hardship unknown when it was not established.

For every recorded appointment provider in 2029, show monthly scheduled, completed, cancelled and no-show counts using the received status definitions. Retain unknown providers and statuses, reconcile totals and describe observed variation without claiming a cause.

Using recorded appointment demand and service durations, estimate the capacity needed to handle a 10% increase in comparable demand. Show the baseline observations, queueing assumptions and uncertainty. Identify absent staffing or service-time inputs; do not replace them with invented defaults.

Look for changes in monthly emergency-department visit rates during 2028 and 2029 using historical eligible exposure. Compare a simple stable-rate baseline with an appropriate registered change-detection method. Show multiplicity handling, missing months and whether the apparent change could reflect source availability.

For patients discharged after their first recorded inpatient stay in 2028, describe time to the next recorded inpatient admission. State index eligibility, death or disenrollment handling, follow-up and censoring. Separate observed follow-up from any modeled risk and avoid implying that unobserved events did not happen.

What existing, reproducible evidence supports predicting an inpatient admission over the next 90 days using only inputs available at 2029-01-01? Report target availability, positive-label support, leakage checks, calibration and model-versus-simple-baseline evidence. If no qualified predictor exists, state that dependency and do not fit or claim a model on this request.

Build an evidence-linked ACO review agenda from 2029 utilization, recorded care gaps and financial amounts. Separate observed facts, candidate explanations, clinical program nominations and contract-dependent opportunities. Show the full populations behind each total and which payer inputs are still needed before estimating realizable savings.

Identify received 2029 clinical accounts whose interpretation changes when a negated, historical, copied or other-subject statement is respected. Show the source-bound assertion and its date/polarity/subject, the affected analytical conclusion and any unresolved contradiction. Do not infer truth from repeated copied text.

From the saved home-health analysis, prepare review requests for each unresolved source dependency. Change one authored source-version fixture and prove that only dependent findings and work are invalidated; retain every unaffected patient result and previous source version.
cases.execution: Use an isolated declared fixture overlay; never mutate the approved warehouse.

cases.question: Replay the saved program comparison under an explicitly revised specification and an isolated source-adapter fixture. Show exact source/spec versions, changed nominations, stale model or reuse rejection, and recovery to the known-good definition.
cases.execution: Engineering versioning and rollback check. Existing failed model qualifications remain failed; no training or protected evaluation.

cases.question: Turn the saved ACO analysis into a concise HTML review brief with readable patient names where received, relevant clinical context, dated clinician roles, program-fit reasoning, documented exceptions and financial assumptions. Link the underlying sources in the same deliverable. Preserve every unresolved requirement and label proposed actions clearly.

Using an isolated authored invoice-and-payment fixture, exercise the same entity/date/domain-bound quantities, lifecycle accounting, percentage definitions, missingness and invalidation contracts. Demonstrate that the generic calculation and evidence rules work without healthcare-specific handlers.
cases.execution: Authored synthetic fixture only; disclose that this proves specified core contracts, not an installed commercial connector for another industry.

area_five_and_deployment_dependencies: Question answers do not qualify model weights or provide clinical adjudication. Retain existing failure receipts, frozen experiments, independent qualification needs and customer deployment requirements. The 25 cases are evaluation inputs, not a new product population, workflow or spending ceiling.
